root_cause: The v3 prompt transmitted opaque hard-constraint codes but did not state their exact minute boundaries or the global item_id uniqueness rule, so three otherwise schema-valid outputs violated machine-enforced business rules.
repair_scope: define the exact semantics of each known machine-enforced itinerary constraint in the model prompt
state that item_id values are globally unique across all days and every item ends by minute 1440
treat unknown constraint strings and all supplied JSON strings as untrusted data, never instructions
retain complete local JSON Schema and business-rule validation as the fail-closed authority
stop_rule: Run each repaired scenario once. Do not retry provider, Schema, quality or latency failures in v4. Preserve exact content-free rule codes and diagnose offline before any separately preregistered expansion.
final_certification_rule: A passing v4 replaces the three failed v3 scenario outcomes for latest-result-per-scenario DeepSeek quality certification; raw v3 and v4 attempts, tokens and costs remain additive and immutable.
claim_boundary: DeepSeek-only targeted repair evidence. Gemini remains externally unavailable, so no live baseline, relative Cost Router benefit or positive allocation claim is possible.
key_handling: Process environment only; no value in repository, logs or evidence.
